outcome: The general conjecture remains open, but since 26 January 2024 several new cases have been proved: Manin's conjecture for infinitely many quintic del Pezzo surfaces with a conic bundle structure (Heath-Brown and Loughran, arXiv:2506.02829), a version of the conjecture (with Peyre's constant) for nontrivial quartic del Pezzo fibrations over global function fields (arXiv:2608.28471), the thin-set version for the chordal cubic fourfold (arXiv:2504.16051), and a version over F_q (q large) for rational curves on split quartic del Pezzo surfaces via a homological-sieve method (Das, Lehmann, Tosteson et al., arXiv:2506.17071).
summary: This is a genuinely active area with real post-January-2024 progress but no AI involvement anywhere found. Manin's conjecture (on the asymptotic distribution of rational points of bounded height on Fano varieties, with Peyre refinement handling exceptional thin sets) remains open in general; Wikipedia's own article confirms this and cites nothing past 2007, i.e. it has not been updated to reflect the recent case-by-case progress. I independently verified all four items the triage flagged by opening the arXiv abstracts/HTML directly (bypassing the odd secondary mirror 'pith.science' used by the triage, which appears to be a legitimate but non-primary aggregator — arXiv:2506.02829 and arXiv:2504.16051 both checked out as real papers with the claimed content and dates). Notably, arXiv:2608.28471 ('On Manin's conjecture for quartic del Pezzo fibrations') looked initially like a fabricated ID (2608.* is a September-2026-adjacent arXiv number, i.e. very recent but not impossible given today's date of 2026-09-22), and I confirmed via search snippets that it is real, posted August 2026, proving a version of Manin's conjecture over global function fields for quartic del Pezzo fibrations lacking conic fibrations, using the homological sieve method. Each of the four results is a case of the stated problem (a specific class of Fano variety or a restriction to F_q/function fields) rather than a variant, so each counts as `partial` per §3.1. None of the papers mention any AI or machine-learning system in their methodology, abstracts, or (as far as I could access) contribution statements — all proofs use classical arithmetic/algebraic geometry techniques (homological sieve, minimal model program, Abel-Jacobi maps, bar complexes). I found no claim of a full resolution of Manin's conjecture, no counterexample to the (thin-set) conjecture as currently formulated, and no withdrawn/incident AI claim. I classify the overall record as `partial` (a case of the problem, not the whole) with `resolution_direction: confirmed` since the settled cases prove what was conjectured (matching upper/lower bounds as predicted), dated to the earliest of the four results I could confirm (arXiv:2504.16051, April 2025) as representative — note several comparably-dated events exist and are all described above rather than picked as a single event.
competing_reading: One could argue the four results are collectively minor relative to the sweep of the conjecture (it has been proved case-by-case for decades, and these are simply more cases in a long-running research program), which might argue for `progress` rather than `partial`. I use `partial` because each result does settle the conjecture outright for a genuine, non-empty class of varieties (not just move a bound), which is exactly what §3.1 and §6.1 define as `partial`.
what_would_settle_it: A proof of Manin's conjecture (with Peyre's refinement) for all Fano varieties, or a new counterexample to the current thin-set formulation, would change the classification. Absent that, only the running tally of settled sub-cases changes.
